intro:
I’m Kevwe, a games programmer focused on gameplay and player-facing systems. Through my degree and personal projects, I’ve worked with Unity, Unreal Engine and standalone C++ frameworks across gameplay, physics, animation and graphics programming.  
I’m particularly interested in where programming and game design meet: how mechanics, movement, level context and feedback shape what players understand and choose to do. I love exploring how the same core mechanic could be used to create very different ways of playing a game, then building the systems that make those ideas feel clear and responsive. Games have created some of my most memorable experiences, and I want to help create that feeling for other players.

development.title: Core Gameplay
development.description: Designing and implementing movement, interactions and abilities that create meaningful choices and shape moment-to-moment play.

development.title: Game Physics
development.description: Using collision, forces and constraints as gameplay tools, balancing physical behaviour with clarity, control and responsiveness.

development.title: Player Feedback and UI
development.description: Using UI, audio, animation and visual feedback to communicate game state and make interaction outcomes clear.

development.title: Graphics Programming
development.description: Experimenting with shaders and real-time rendering techniques, particularly lighting, skeletal animation and procedural effects.

working.label: Codebase Awareness
working.value: I follow established conventions and understand the existing architecture before making changes.

working.label: Player-Centred Systems Thinking
working.value: I consider both how a feature interacts with surrounding systems and what it asks the player to understand, decide and do.

working.label: Adaptability
working.value: I’m comfortable learning unfamiliar libraries, engines and frameworks.

working.label: Team Communication
working.value: I can explain technical decisions clearly and compromise when it supports the shared result.

games.title: Hades II
games.note: I like how its progression systems give the player meaningful control over how each run develops, and how it uses RNG to introduce variation.

games.title: Disco Elysium
games.note: Its detailed world-building and branching dialogue make choices feel personal through an accumulation of small-scale consequences.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
games.note: Its restrained guidance makes exploration feel self-directed and consistently rewards curiosity.
